- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact to upward momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for 30d horizon if bullish sentiment persists.
- If model shows gradual upward trend (e.g., +0.1–0.3 per day) but true outcome spikes sharply (e.g., +5+ points), reduce forecast slope after spike to avoid overshoot.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low (≤0.3), model often underestimates price rise; add 2–5% buffer to forecast if supply net < -10 and sentiment ≤0.3.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.0) after a spike, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion rule: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast if sentiment drops below 0.0.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14d moving average, adjust forecast to align with 14d MA unless sentiment strongly bullish (≥0.8) or bearish (≤0.2) — in which case allow deviation.
- If multiple consecutive days show high bullish sentiment (≥0.8) and model forecast is flat or declining, force upward adjustment by 1–2% per day to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- If model forecast is >10% above 14d MA and sentiment is neutral or bearish, apply downward correction by 1–3% per day to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If supply net is negative and sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5), model often underestimates price; add 1–3% to forecast if supply net < -10 and sentiment ≤0.5.
